topicName: Deployment Architectures (Vercel, Self-Hosting with Docker, Standalone Output)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Deployment Architectures in Next.js: Vercel, Docker, and Standalone Output"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choosing the right deployment architecture for a Next.js application depends heavily on your performance requirements, scalability needs, and infrastructure constraints. Next.js offers extreme flexibility, supporting zero-config serverless deployments, containerized environments, and traditional server setups."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Zero-Config Deployment on Vercel"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Vercel is created by the creators of Next.js and provides the most optimized environment for running Next.js applications. It abstracts away server management by utilizing a serverless and edge architecture."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Automatic HTTPS, global CDN integration, and zero-configuration setups."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) and Edge Functions work out of the box."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Preview deployments generated automatically for every Pull Request."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Standalone Output Mode"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"For self-hosting or custom containerized environments, Next.js provides a standalone output mode. This automatically traces your application to leverage only the necessary files and node_modules required for production, drastically reducing the final image or bundle size."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"module.exports = { output: 'standalone' }"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"When you run 'next build' with this configuration, Next.js outputs a folder at '.next/standalone' containing a minimal Node.js server script alongside your compiled application."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Self-Hosting with Docker"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Containerizing a Next.js application using Docker ensures consistent behavior across different environments. By utilizing the standalone output, you can build a lightweight, production-ready container image."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"FROM node:18-alpine AS base

WORKDIR /app

FROM base AS builder
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . . 
RUN npm run build

FROM base AS runner
ENV NODE_ENV=production
RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs
RUN adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs

COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static

USER nextjs
EXPOSE 3000
ENV PORT=3000
ENV HOSTNAME="0.0.0.0"

CMD ["node", "server.js"]"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you want minimal operational overhead and advanced edge features, Vercel is the optimal choice. If your organization requires strict on-premise infrastructure control, utilizing Docker combined with the Next.js standalone output mode provides a secure, lightweight, and highly performant architecture."}]
